claims.claim: The Wardenclyffe tower was 187 feet tall.
claims.quote: By the end of 1902 the tower reached its full height of 187 feet.

claims.claim: The tower never became operational.
claims.quote: Additional investment could not be found, and the project was abandoned in 1906, never to become operational.

claims.claim: The 1904 photo was taken so Tesla could go back to J. P. Morgan to ask for money to finish the tower.
claims.quote: This 1904 photo of Wardenclyffe was taken so that Tesla could go back to J. P. Morgan to try and get the additional funds he needed to finish the tower.

claims.claim: The 1904 file's author is unknown and it is public domain.
claims.quote:
Author: Unknown author Unknown author
Licence: Public domain

claims.claim: Tesla was not sending radio waves; he doubted Hertzian waves existed and thought that if they did they would travel straight into space and be "hopelessly lost."
claims.quote: Tesla doubted they existed and he followed scientific thought of the period that, if they did exist, this was just a type of invisible light which would travel in straight lines the way visible light did, meaning they would travel straight out into space and be "hopelessly lost".

claims.claim: Tesla's plan was to drive current into the Earth and use the planet itself as the conductor.
claims.quote: (using) the Earth itself as the medium for conducting the currents, thus dispensing with wires and all other artificial conductors

claims.claim: File:US patent 1119732-001.png is a diagram by Nikola Tesla, public domain.
claims.quote:

Date: (none recorded)
Author: Nikola Tesla

claims.claim: A wood and steel lined shaft was sunk 120 feet beneath the tower, per descriptions including Tesla's 1923 foreclosure testimony.
claims.quote: The descriptions (some from Tesla's 1923 testimony in foreclosure proceedings on the property) include that the facility had a ten by twelve foot wood and steel lined shaft sunk into the ground 120 feet (37 m) beneath the tower with a stairway inside it.

claims.claim: At the bottom of the shaft, machines pushed sixteen iron pipes out 300 feet.
claims.quote: I pushed these iron pipes, I think sixteen of them, three hundred feet, and then the current through these pipes takes hold of the earth.

claims.claim: Tesla said the purpose was "to have a grip on the earth so the whole of this globe can quiver."
claims.quote: In Tesla's words, the function of this was "to have a grip on the earth so the whole of this globe can quiver".

claims.claim: File:Wardenclyffe Tower.jpg is circa 1902 with no recorded author, public domain.
claims.quote:

claims.claim: Tesla wrote asking Morgan whether he would help or let "my great work — almost complete — go to pots."
claims.quote: In a July 3, 1903 letter Tesla wrote "Will you help me or let my great work — almost complete — go to pots?"

claims.claim: Morgan replied on July 14 that he was not disposed to make further advances.
claims.quote: Morgan's reply on July 14 was "I have received your letter and in reply would say that I should not feel disposed at present to make any further advances".

claims.claim: Newspapers reported that on the night of Morgan's reply and several nights after, the tower shot off bright flashes lighting up the sky.
claims.quote: The night of Morgan's reply, and several nights after, newspapers reported that the Wardenclyffe tower came alive shooting off bright flashes lighting up the night sky.

claims.claim: No explanation of the flashes ever came from Tesla or his workers.
claims.quote: No explanation was forthcoming from Tesla or any of his workers as to the meaning of the display and Wardenclyffe never seemed to operate again.

claims.claim: The scrap value realized was $1,750.
claims.quote: The scrap value realized was $1,750 (equivalent to $44,000 in 2025).

claims.claim: The Smiley Steel Company of New York began demolition on July 4, 1917 by dynamiting the tower.
claims.quote: On July 4, 1917, the Smiley Steel Company of New York began demolition of the tower by dynamiting it.

claims.claim: The first blast only knocked the tower onto a tilt; it was not fully demolished until September.
claims.quote: The tower was knocked on a tilt by the initial explosion but it was not totally demolished until September.

claims.claim: A wartime rumor said the government ordered the tower destroyed because of German spies.
claims.quote: a rumor spread, picked up by newspapers and other publications, that the tower was demolished on orders of the United States Government with claims German spies were using it as a radio transmitter or observation post

claims.claim: The real reason for the demolition was foreclosure.
claims.quote: When Tesla was unable to make any further payments on the mortgages, Boldt foreclosed on the Wardenclyffe property. Boldt went on to make the property available for sale and decided to demolish the tower for scrap.

claims.claim: Tesla could not correct the rumor because the mortgages and foreclosure had been kept off the public record to hide his financial difficulties.
claims.quote: but since the original mortgages with Boldt as well as the foreclosure had been kept off the public record in order to hide his financial difficulties, Tesla was not able to reveal the real reason for the demolition.

claims.claim: The demolition photograph is attributed to the American Press Association and is public domain.
claims.quote:
Author: attributed to the "American Press Association"
Licence: Public domain

claims.claim: Tesla kept the press and public away from the site, so little is known about what was built underground.
claims.quote: There was a great deal of construction under the tower to establish some form of ground connection, but Tesla and his workers kept the public and the press away from the project, so little is known.

claims.claim: Descriptions mention four 100-foot tunnels radiating from the shaft.
claims.quote: There is also contemporaneous and later descriptions of four 100 foot long tunnels, possibly brick lined and waterproofed, radiating from the bottom of the shaft north, south, east, and west terminating back at ground level in little brick igloos.

claims.claim: Speculation about the tunnels includes drainage, access, or enhancing ground connection, possibly filled with salt water or liquid nitrogen.
claims.quote: Speculation on the tunnels ranges from them being for drainage, acting as access ways, or having the function of enhancing ground connection or resonance by interacting with the water table below the tower, maybe via being filled with salt water or liquid nitrogen.

claims.claim: How Tesla intended to combine the ground conduction and atmospheric methods at Wardenclyffe is unknown.
claims.quote: How Tesla intended to employ the ground conduction method and atmospheric method in Wardenclyffe's design is unknown.

claims.claim: In March 1901 J. P. Morgan signed a contract giving Tesla $150,000 to build a wireless station on Long Island capable of sending messages to London and to ships at sea.
claims.quote: Morgan signed a contract with Tesla in March 1901, agreeing to give the inventor $150,000 ($5.81 million in 2025) to develop and build a wireless station on Long Island, capable of sending wireless messages to London as well as ships at sea.

claims.claim: Morgan took a 51% interest in the company and in the patents.
claims.quote: The deal also included Morgan having a 51% interest in the company as well as a 51% share in present and future wireless patents developed from the project.

claims.claim: Tesla wanted to inject current into the ground at the right frequency and make the whole planet resonate.
claims.quote: He theorized from these experiments that if he injected electric current into the Earth at just the right frequency he could harness what he believed was the planet's own electrical charge and cause it to resonate at a frequency that would be amplified in "standing waves"

claims.claim: Tesla read a June 1901 article by Marconi and decided to scale everything up with a more powerful transmitter, image and telephone transmission, and wireless power.
claims.quote: Tesla's plans changed radically after he read a June 1901 Electrical Review article by Marconi titled "Syntonic Wireless Telegraph".

claims.claim: Morgan refused additional funds and demanded an accounting of what had been spent.
claims.quote: With Tesla basically proposing a breach of contract, Morgan refused to lend additional funds and demanded an account of money already spent.

claims.claim: The project was abandoned in 1906.
claims.quote: Additional investment could not be found, and the project was abandoned in 1906, never to become operational.
